stories.title: U.S. Designates Palestinian Refugee in Germany as “Terrorist”
stories.text: The U.S. has designated a stateless Palestinian refugee based in Germany as a “terrorist,” alongside three European-linked left-wing groups. On Wednesday, the Office of Foreign Assets Control placed 30-year-old Zaid Abdulnasser on the list of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons as one of two alleged “leaders or officials” of Masar Badil. The designation falls under Executive Order 13224, issued by President George W. Bush after 9/11. In its statement on Palestine Action, Masar Badil, and Autistici Inventati, the Treasury Department described Masar Badil as a “front organization” for the Samidoun Palestinian Prisoner Solidarity Network, which Washington sanctioned in October 2024. Samidoun, the department says, is controlled by the leftist Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, which the U.S. has designated a “terrorist organization” since 1997. In an exclusive interview, Abdulnasser, who has a six-month-old child, told Drop Site he was shocked when friends sent him the press release announcing the designation. “I was frightened. stories.author: Ken Klippenstein
stories.title: Dolly Parton’s Superpower
stories.text: Subscribe Dolly Parton had a power no president does: the ability to influence basically anyone for the better. "I am not political,” she once famously said. “I'm more about the person and about the message.” Compare that to the brute force logic of our politics, where the prevailing strategy is to win the White House, run up the score in Congress, and bulldoze the opposition. Parton showed another way. In a world of team red and team blue, Dolly was platinum . She understood that the most valuable substance is consensus; and like platinum, it’s precious because it’s rare. It can’t be forced and must be gathered with patience and care. Dolly managed this by walking a tightrope. An early defender of gay marriage, she made her case not by shaming opponents but with playful self-deprecation, quipping: “Why shouldn’t they get to be as miserable as the rest of us?” She was a philanthropist but didn’t virtue signal, instead preferring to remain anonymous. For decades, Parton anonymously covered the cost of school band uniforms at high schools across Tennessee, never publicizing the gesture or attaching her name to it. stories.title: A Natural Gas Astroturf Group Says It Flipped NY Gov. Hochul
stories.text: In November 2025, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul pulled an about-face on climate policy that caused a furor among the state’s environmentalists . Once an opponent of new fossil fuel infrastructure, the governor announced she would approve a new Trump-backed gas pipeline project that had previously been rejected by state officials. She called the new strategy an “all of the above” approach to energy, invoking voter concerns about “grid reliability and affordability.” What Hochul didn’t say was that her new posture came weeks after her office met with a gas industry front group funded and deeply tied to the company behind the long-delayed pipeline project, according to industry materials reviewed by The Lever . At a fossil fuel industry conference in April, the pipeline-backed group Natural Allies for a Clean Energy Future took credit for Hochul’s change of heart, boasting of “high-level engagement” with her office. stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Measles, Mamdani, and MAGA Inc.
stories.text: Michael Whatley, the Republican nominee for Senate in North Carolina, released an ad stating that he has “driven thousands of miles across North Carolina trying to fix our country and help working families.” But campaign finance filings reveal that Whatley’s campaign committees have spent over $100,000 since last September on travel in a $2 million private jet. A paper trail links these payments to a felon convicted of defrauding the federal government. Opponents of California’s proposed billionaire tax are running an ad falsely claiming that the initiative would require everyone to itemize and report all their assets to the state. The ad was sponsored by Californians Against Wasteful Spending and Higher Taxes, a project of the California Business Roundtable (CBRT). CBRT’s PAC is funded by several billionaires, including Peter Thiel. The New York Post has repeatedly claimed that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani “doxxed” wealthy New Yorkers by publishing a property ownership list last month as the city implements the new pied-à-terre tax. stories.title: Do Rural Residents Have the Power to Say No?
stories.text: This piece by Raj Patel, a research professor at the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs and a member of the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems, and Jim Goodman, a retired dairy farmer, looks at the way hyperscalers are approaching the construction of data centers in rural communities and the rights those communities have. The piece is part of Drop Site’s ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser to put a focus on rural politics with a newsletter running through November. Story by Raj Patel and Jim Goodman Today’s data center proponents argue that such projects bring needed jobs and a boost to local economies. Rural America has heard confident pitches like these before. Nearly 40 years ago, concentrated animal feeding operations ( CAFOs ) arrived one barn at a time with bold promises of jobs and a county tax base. By the time neighbors organized, right-to-farm laws and state preemption had cut the ground from under them. All the while, manure lagoons leached into the groundwater and fouled the air, shortening the life expectancy of the farmworkers and downwind neighbors.
